pixel_description: Photoreal side view of wheeled rover on dark soil strip, light background. Front left: spiked cutting-drum disc in soil pile with side arm bolted to chassis; just behind it a spiked grouser front wheel partially hidden by arm, under front of dark low-profile horizontal frame. Tall silver perception mast bolted to front top of frame with diagonal folding brace, topped by stacked camera head with multiple lenses plus antenna boxes. Mid-frame: large black battery box with small top box and antenna, cable to smaller control and radio box with antenna rear-mid, both sitting on frame. Rear: large spiked grouser wheel under frame, vertical rear high-lift mast bolted to frame above wheel. Critical part Rear high-lift mast (lift) is drawn as one visible light-gray vertical guide column with bolted foot to chassis and pivot bolts at top, one visible black hydraulic actuator cylinder parallel inboard, one visible vertical roller chain outboard with top sprocket/pinion under hopper and bottom roller above frame, second column/actuator hidden by side-view occlusion. Large open metal hopper pivoted on top of guide, tilted rear-down, pouring continuous soil stream into black open collection bin sitting on rear frame extension behind wheel. Frame length ~3x wheel diameter, wheels ~300mm class, lift raises hopper ~3x wheel diameter to ~1.05m lip with rear overhang. Short callout labels with leader lines present.

s1_differences: No mechanism difference; same parts, connections, relative sizes, orientations and dump direction as labeled sketch in deployed high-lift pose. Only depiction differences are callout labels containing disallowed numbers/sizes.
s2_feedback: No design flaw visible: rear guide, actuator cylinder and chain are clear of wheel and frame, hopper pivot clears mast and pours into bin behind with front axle still loaded, drum arm clears soil, mast foot and cable routing reachable. Deployed geometry matches 1.05m lip/0.30m overhang intent without interference or impossible load path.
notes: Segmenter gaps/touches are coarse-mask artifacts and side-view occlusion in deployed dump pose. Mechanism itself matches sketch. Only faults to redraw are callout labels containing numbers/sizes/units, which are depiction faults with part_id callout and do not change working principle.
